rounds.text: Roadstar Infra Investment Trust is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround that is not yet reflected in its valuation. The company has demonstrated a massive surge in profitability, with quarterly operating margins jumping to 68% in June 2026 from 17% in the year-ago quarter [E20], and net profit growth reaching 128% year-over-year [E46]. This momentum is supported by strong cash generation, evidenced by Rs 849 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 797 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E24, E25]. Despite this improving performance, the stock remains undervalued, trading at a price-to-book ratio of 0.71x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 8.01x, which is notably lower than the sector benchmark of 10.19x [E10]. Furthermore, the company is actively strengthening its balance sheet by reducing total borrowings from Rs 3,669 Cr to Rs 3,306 Cr [E28]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with low return on equity [E12, E18, E51], inconsistent operating margins [E21, E22], and a low interest coverage ratio [E43]. Investors should note that current results are accelerating, with profit growth now exceeding one-year price growth, suggesting the market may be relying on stale sentiment rather than the current trajectory [E40, E52].

Roadstar Infra Investment Trust exhibits persistent structural inefficiencies, evidenced by a negative return on equity of -6.83% [E8] and a median three-year return on equity of -2% [E17]. The company’s operational performance is highly inconsistent, with operating margins fluctuating significantly and declining from 62% to 50% over the last three years [E19, E21, E22]. Furthermore, the business struggles to generate adequate returns on its capital, with an ROCE of only 2.13% compared to a sector benchmark of 6.66% [E9]. This fundamental weakness is compounded by a low interest coverage ratio [E43] and extreme annualised volatility of 53.0% [E37], which results in a negligible Sharpe ratio of 0.03 [E38]. Conceded: the company maintains a comfortable current ratio of 2.16x [E27], shows strong recent quarterly margin expansion [E20], and trades at a discount to book value [E1, E42]. Despite these liquidity and valuation metrics, the underlying inability to consistently generate positive shareholder returns remains a significant risk to the investment thesis [E12, E18, E51].

The bear focuses on negative historical returns on equity, but the turnaround is already underway as results score an impressive 81 out of 100 with net profit surging 128% year-over-year [E52]. Conceded: the three-year median return on equity is -2% [E17] and trailing ROE is -6.83% [E8], but looking backward dismisses the massive operational inflection seen in the recent quarter where operating margin skyrocketed to 68% compared to just 17% a year ago [E20]. While the bear highlights an inconsistent multi-year operating margin trend [E21, E22] and a drop in TTM margins [E19], it completely ignores the substantial cash generation firepower, featuring an operating cash flow of ₹ 849 Cr and free cash flow of ₹ 797 Cr for Mar 2026 [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the bear's cited ROCE concerns [E9] are offset by a strong balance sheet showing reduced borrowings down to ₹ 3,306 Cr [E28] and a comfortable current ratio of 2.16x [E27]. Finally, the bear warns of low interest coverage [E43] and high volatility [E37], yet overlooks that the market is severely under-appreciating the asset base by pricing the stock at a steep discount to book value at 0.71x [E1] alongside an attractive 8.69% dividend yield [E3].

Conceded: the company posted a net profit increase of 128% year-over-year [E46, E52] and generated ₹ 849 Cr in operating cash flow for Mar 2026 [E24]. However, the bull's narrative of an operational inflection is undermined by the company's officially flagged low interest coverage ratio [E43] and an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend over the last two years [E21]. While the bull points to reduced borrowings of ₹ 3,306 Cr [E28], the fundamental profitability remains deeply negative, with trailing ROE sitting at -6.83% against a sector benchmark of 5.13% [E8] and a three-year median ROE of -2.09% [E44]. The heavy reliance on a discounted book value of 0.71x [E1] and an 8.69% dividend yield [E3] fails to offset chronic capital inefficiency, evidenced by an annualised volatility of 53.0% [E37], a negligible Sharpe ratio of 0.03 [E38], and a sector-lagging ROCE of just 2.13% [E9].
